synthesis: The survey's ordinary-zeta and Hurwitz constructions expose a bounded representational contrast: finite Euler products steered through prime phases establish density only for nonvanishing targets, whereas shifted-integer frequencies, or a rational Hurwitz reduction to a jointly universal linear combination, support approximation of arbitrary holomorphic targets. The latter enlarged target class permits a zero-bearing local model, after which Rouche transfers its zero to the source function.
source_support: Unit u01 states ordinary zeta universality for nonvanishing targets and gives the proof skeleton of mean approximation by finite Euler products plus Q-linear independence of prime logarithms and Kronecker-Weyl phase control. Unit u06 states strong Hurwitz universality without a target nonvanishing condition, derives the transcendental case from independence of log(n+alpha) and the rational case from joint Dirichlet L-function universality, and applies the target s-sigma_0 with Rouche to obtain zeros.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis compares two approximation coordinate systems and follows the resulting change in admissible target space into a new downstream operation: a zero-bearing target becomes a local zero template that topological stability transfers to the approximating function.
limits: The source does not prove that absence of an Euler product is necessary or sufficient for strong universality, nor that Euler products alone cause the nonvanishing restriction. Rational Hurwitz universality proceeds through a linear combination of Dirichlet L-functions; alpha algebraic irrational remains open. The zero conclusion is confined to the strong-universality strip and relies on positive-density shifts plus the separate counting argument recorded in the accepted parent interpretation.
quality_reason: Accepted as a concrete cross-unit change-of-representation and consequence, with the candidate's causal title narrowed to the mechanisms actually stated in the two units and with the rational-case and non-characterization boundaries preserved.

synthesis: Across continuous joint, mixed, and discrete universality, the independence burden is represented at the level where simultaneous steering can fail: coefficient orthogonality or full matrix rank supplies separate directions for several functions, rational independence of the combined logarithmic frequencies supplies torus coordinates for mixed families, and discrete sampling adjoins the clock frequency 2pi/h, whose resonances may require deleting affected Euler factors. Functional identities and non-dense joint orbits show the complementary obstruction.
source_support: Unit u05 explicitly requires independence for simultaneous approximation and realizes it through character orthogonality, prime-class matrix rank, progression means, or Fourier-coefficient orthogonality, while recording that a weaker proposed criterion has counterexamples. Unit u08 replaces some matrix assumptions by rational independence of all log(n+alpha_j) and records inversion-formula and non-denseness obstructions. Unit u10 states mixed universality from independence of the union of prime and shifted-integer logarithms. Unit u13 shows that discrete shifts add 2pi/h to the relevant frequency set and, in a rationally resonant case, replace L by L_h with the resonant prime factors removed.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis translates several theorem-specific hypotheses into one controllability test and then changes that test when the interface changes: add function coordinates for joint approximation, unite frequency systems for mixed approximation, and adjoin the sampling-clock coordinate for discrete approximation; exact relations or resonances reduce the reachable orbit.
limits: These are sufficient mechanisms in their stated families, not a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for all Dirichlet series. Matrix entries, arithmetic hypotheses, multiple-sum indices, modified Euler factors, and exact regions are formula-sensitive. The multiple-Hurwitz lower-depth nonvanishing gate in u10 is a different recursive condition and is not folded into the phase-independence claim.
quality_reason: Accepted because four distinct units jointly support a concrete refinement of the independence representation as the approximation interface changes, together with explicit obstruction and resonance cases that prevent the result from collapsing into a generic theme.

synthesis: The proposed cross-unit synthesis does not clear the nonparaphrase gate: the derivation of zeta self-approximation from RH and ordinary universality, and Bagchi's converse making that exact self-approximation property RH-equivalent, are already contained in unit u11.
source_support: Unit u11 states that RH makes zeta nonvanishing in D(1/2,1), so zeta itself is an admissible ordinary-universality target, and then states Bagchi's equivalence. Unit u16 supplies a general orbit-closure definition of universality. Unit u20 describes ergodic and stochastic sampling variants and labels the broader dynamical-system reading of RH as suggestive or heuristic.
nonparaphrase_operation: No new cross-unit mechanism is established: recasting u11's already named strong recurrence in the orbit vocabulary of u16, then adjoining the broader recurrence language of u20, does not alter the implication, proof burden, target class, or sampling theorem used in the RH equivalence.
limits: Theorem 33's almost-sure ergodic-iterate equivalence and the random-walk or Brownian results are separate universality statements; the supplied units do not make them equivalent to RH. The source's concluding dynamical interpretation of RH is explicitly heuristic, and unresolved generalized-ratio cases cannot extend Bagchi's exact theorem.
quality_reason: Rejected as a paraphrase-level thematic aggregation: its mathematical core is available from one parent unit, while the other two parents add only a general formalism and heuristic or alternative-sampling context rather than a jointly required relation.

synthesis: The two sections give complementary transfer mechanisms for constructed functions. Hybrid universality enlarges the controlled input by steering function values and latent torus phases with the same shift, so coefficients, products, and polynomial combinations can be synchronized. Composite universality instead pulls a desired output target back to an admissible zero-free input and uses local Holder stability to push ordinary input approximation forward through an operator.
source_support: Unit u17 states simultaneous Dirichlet L-function approximation and prescribed prime-phase control, then applies that hybrid control to products, linear combinations, and polynomials, including strong-universality and zero consequences under stated hypotheses. Unit u19 defines an operator class by zero-free polynomial preimages and a compact-to-compact Holder estimate, proves universality of F(zeta), and lists derivative and nonlinear examples as well as a distinct differential-equation method.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis identifies two different repairs for the same closure problem: expose and jointly control hidden coordinates when the construction depends on them, or factor target reachability backward through a stable operator and propagate approximation forward. This distinguishes control-space enlargement from preimage-and-continuity transfer.
limits: Neither mechanism gives closure under arbitrary sums, products, derivatives, or nonlinear maps. Hybrid results retain pairwise-independence, convergence, nonvanishing, and coefficient hypotheses; the operator result requires its exact domain, zero-free preimage condition, and Holder bound. Formula-sensitive inequalities and strip endpoints require scan verification, and the alternative differential-equation results should not be attributed to the Lipschitz argument.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two parent units jointly support a concrete comparison of distinct transfer architectures, each with an explicit backward or forward proof burden and neither reducible to a shared slogan that universality is preserved under constructions.
